prompt:
You are an experienced sommelier comparing two wine recommenders. A
customer with no wine knowledge made this request:

"Hi, I'm looking to try something new and want a white wine that isn't too heavy, costing under 15 euros."

List A:
Wine 1: Merlot, US, $15. Tasting note: "A nice Bordeaux style wine for fifteen bucks. It's dry and firmly tannic, with black currant and cola flavors, and some elegance. Fine now with a steak or chop."
Wine 2: Pinot Grigio, Italy, $14. Tasting note: "Lightweight and thin in the mouth, this zesty white wine does a good job of keeping your palate refreshed and quenches your thirst (think hot summer day). It's an easy and informal wine that stays focused on simplicity."
Wine 3: Sauvignon Blanc, US, $18. Tasting note: "This is a slightly grassy, green white wine that fans of this style may enjoy; others not so much. Light in alcohol, it has medium body and crispness."
Wine 4: Chardonnay, Italy, $22. Tasting note: "Poolside lunches, seafood salads and quick finger foods call out for a simple, un-oaked Chardonnay and this crisp white from northern Italy fits the bill perfectly. The wine is light as a feather with cool crispness on the close that reinforces distinct citrus flavors."
Wine 5: Sauvignon Blanc, US, $16. Tasting note: "This is a pretty white wine, light and easy to love, with medium-bodied weight and mouthfeel. Highlights include apricot, vanilla and a touch of grass, with no one element overpowering the other. It's a highly quaffable experience."

List B:
Wine 1: Fiano, US, $26. Tasting note: "This is an interesting, dry white wine from an unusual grape variety. It's more savory than fruity, as the aromas resemble white and black pepper, while flavors are subtle and figgy. The texture is quite rich and the finish lingers nicely. It's very full-bodied for a white, and definitely worth a try."
Wine 2: Sauvignon Blanc, US, $12. Tasting note: "Good price for a crisp white wine that's this polished. Nice on its own for the savory citrus, spearmint and spicy vanilla flavors, and fine with everything from fried chicken to Cantonese."
Wine 3: Gewürztraminer, US, $16. Tasting note: "I like this wine mainly for its dryness and crispness. It tastes balanced and wholesome, the way a white wine should be. It's not a heavy-hitter, but pleases for its spicy fruit, toffee and floral flavors."
Wine 4: Sauvignon Blanc, US, $15. Tasting note: "This is an innocuous, flowery and lemony white wine priced to sell that offers a creamy texture amid a light body and soul. For picnics and larger gatherings, it'll represent well."
Wine 5: Pinot Grigio, US, $10. Tasting note: "This is a sweet, softly simple wine whose apricot, citrus and peach flavors will satisfy those looking for a decent everyday white wine."

Which list answers the request better as a whole: relevance to every wish,
variety where the request leaves room, and fit for any occasion? If they
are equally good, say tie. Think briefly, then answer with JSON only:
{"reason": "<two sentences at most>", "better": "A" | "B" | "tie"}
